plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp boxing build with a little extra conditioning, using bodyweight-only training and beginner-friendly exercise choices. Week 1 establishes simple performance baselines on the main primary patterns so future progress is easier to track, and the main build starts in Week 2. The block emphasizes explosive intent first, then basic strength endurance, then trunk, neck, and short conditioning that should fit around boxing practice without beating you up.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic strength, power, trunk control, and repeat-effort conditioning with simple bodyweight methods.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the same movement patterns with harder variations and slightly denser conditioning while keeping form sharp.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Turn the strength base into faster, crisper boxing-relevant power and conditioning with lower fatigue.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can on every rep. Reset between reps and land softly.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if squat jumps irritate the knees. Keep the landing quiet and controlled.

exercises.name: 1b. Broad Jump
exercises.notes: Stick each landing for a full second. Stop the set if distance drops off clearly.

substitutionOptions.name: Snap Down to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if broad jumps feel too aggressive. Focus on fast drop and stable landing.

exercises.name: Push-Up Test
exercises.reps: Max clean reps leaving 1 rep in reserve
exercises.notes: This sets a baseline for future progress. Use strict form, full range, and stop before the first ugly rep.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard set of strict push-ups and stop with about one rep left in the tank. Log the reps so the app can track your starting point.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat your best clean rep set over time without losing range or body position.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up Test
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench, table, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are not yet strong enough for clean reps.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a slow lower and stand up hard. Keep the front foot flat and torso tall.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats feel awkward. Step back under control and drive through the front leg.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep low back gently pressed down and ribs tucked. Shorten the lever if you lose position.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if full hollow hold is too hard. Keep every rep slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Neck Flexion Isometric
exercises.notes: Use your hand for light resistance only. Stay smooth and pain free.

substitutionOptions.name: Supine Head Lift Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Lift the head slightly from the floor and hold if manual resistance feels awkward.

exercises.name: Tempo Shadowboxing Intervals
exercises.notes: Move continuously but stay relaxed. Keep every round technical, light on the feet, and nasal-breathing if possible.

exercises.name: 1a. Plyometric Push-Up from Knees
exercises.notes: Push fast so the hands leave the floor slightly. Keep the body braced and land softly.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a sturdy surface and drive up as fast as possible if the floor version is too hard.

exercises.name: 1b. Fast Mountain Climber
exercises.notes: Keep hips level and shoulders stacked. Move quickly without bouncing all over the place.

exercises.name: Inverted Row Test
exercises.reps: Max clean reps leaving 1 rep in reserve
exercises.notes: This sets a baseline for future progress. Use a sturdy setup and stop before body position breaks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard set of strict inverted rows and stop with about one rep left in reserve. Log the reps so the app can track your starting point.

performanceTarget.prompt: Build your best clean row set over time while keeping the body rigid.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if the anchor is very secure. Keep tension high and reps strict.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
exercises.notes: Hands just inside shoulder width. Keep elbows tucked naturally and full-body tension throughout.

substitutionOptions.name: Standard Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the close grip bothers the wrists or shoulders.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Make a straight line from head to heel. Do not let the top hip roll back.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Plank from Knees
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full version is too hard to hold cleanly.

exercises.name: Neck Lateral Isometric
exercises.notes: Use your hand for gentle pressure. Stay tall and avoid shrugging.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall-Supported Neck Side Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Press lightly into a wall if manual resistance is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Shadowboxing Speed Rounds
exercises.notes: Short bursts of fast hands and feet with clean technique. Keep the shoulders loose and recover fully between rounds.

exercises.name: 1a. Skater Hop to Stick
exercises.notes: Jump side to side and own the landing before the next rep. Keep the knee tracking over the foot.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Step and Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hop feels too aggressive. Move quickly and stabilize on each side.

exercises.name: 1b. Pogo Jump
exercises.notes: Stay tall and springy off the ankles. Keep the contacts quick and quiet.

exercises.name: Split Squat Test
exercises.reps: Max clean reps each side leaving 1 rep in reserve
exercises.notes: This sets a baseline for future progress. Use a controlled lower, full range, and stop before balance or depth fails.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard set per side and stop with about one rep left in reserve. Log the reps on each side so the app can track your starting point.

performanceTarget.prompt: Build cleaner, stronger rep sets on both sides without losing depth or balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge Test
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squat setup is uncomfortable. Keep stride length consistent on both sides.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and finish with the glute, not the low back.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the single-leg version cramps or shifts too much.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.notes: Curl the pelvis up gently instead of swinging the legs. Lower under control.

substitutionOptions.name: Bent-Knee Leg Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if reverse crunches are hard to feel in the trunk.

exercises.name: Shuttle Footwork Intervals
exercises.notes: Use quick in-and-out footwork over a short distance. Stay light and sharp rather than turning it into an all-out sprint.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.notes: Move slowly enough to stay controlled. Keep knees low and hips quiet.

substitutionOptions.name: High Plank Shoulder Tap
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if crawling space is limited. Keep the trunk still.

exercises.name: Push-Up Shoulder Tap
exercises.notes: Take a wide enough stance to control the rotation. Move with intent, not speed.

substitutionOptions.name: High Plank Shoulder Tap
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if push-up position reps are too demanding.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
exercises.notes: Use small ranges and squeeze the upper back. Do not shrug the shoulders up.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Slide
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the floor version is awkward. Keep the ribs down.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard and pull the elbows toward the toes without moving.

substitutionOptions.name: Hardstyle Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if plank position bothers the shoulders.

exercises.name: Neck Extension Isometric
exercises.notes: Use light hand resistance and keep the chin slightly tucked. No pain and no jerking.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Head Lift Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Lift the head slightly from the floor and hold if manual resistance is awkward.

exercises.name: Continuous Shadowboxing
exercises.notes: Keep this easy and rhythmic. Use the round to loosen up, breathe, and accumulate light conditioning without extra soreness.
